why: Walk two sorted sequences together, merging. The trick that keeps it in place is to fill nums1 from the back: compare the largest remaining values of the two valid parts and write the larger one into the last free slot, so nothing unread is ever overwritten.
hints: Merging from the front would overwrite values of nums1 you have not read yet. Where is there free space?
The free slots are at the end of nums1. The largest value of the merged result is the larger of nums1[m-1] and nums2[n-1]: write it at position m+n-1.
Pointers i = m-1, j = n-1, w = m+n-1. While j >= 0: if i >= 0 and nums1[i] > nums2[j], write nums1[i] and i -= 1, else write nums2[j] and j -= 1; w -= 1. O(m + n).
pitfalls: m = 0: the answer is just nums2.
Loop until nums2 is exhausted; leftover nums1 values are already in place.
Values can be negative and equal; ties may take from either side.
